text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty p1 triggered: GPU node instability in inference-prod (us-west-2). Symptoms: container OOMs, driver resets, Xid errors. Escalation policy: oncall -> sre.

olivia (oncall): I'm taking this. seeing 3 nodes flapping (gpu-uw2-[13,17,21]). Multiple containers died with signal 9 and driver resets logged.

ashwin: can you paste the XID samples? last night we saw Xid 79 then 43. different banks?

olivia (oncall): logs from node gpu-uw2-13:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568130] kernel: docker: task killed by oom
[ 1234.569000] NVRM: ECC error, single-bit corrected
```

maria: interesting — Xid 79 -> often driver reset after ECC parity event. Are the affected pods pinned to GPUs or running on shared gpus?

leo: those pods use model-serving pool with exclusive GPU allocation (NVIDIA MIG not in use).

olivia (oncall): immediate mitigation: cordon + drain the three nodes to stop new workloads landing. running `kubectl cordon gpu-uw2-13` now.

sre-bot: cordon completed for gpu-uw2-13, gpu-uw2-17, gpu-uw2-21. Drains in progress — evicting pods where possible, honoring PDBs.

ashwin: can we fallback those inference routes to lower-capacity region (us-east-1) or a replica pool? We should avoid customer impact.

jamie (support): I'm flagging affected customer tenants: alpha-suite and beta-saas currently hit increased latency/failures. I'll open a status note if we see >5% error rate sustained.

olivia (oncall): rolling redirect to us-east-1 for high-priority routes: updating traffic policy to prefer region:us-east-1 for model:v2-large via runtime router.

maria: concurrent step — collect `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` dumps before rebooting nodes. driver resets obscure the original ECC state.

olivia (oncall): grabbing dumps now. attaching snippet:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0:
  ECC Errors:
    Volatile:  Corrected: 245, Uncorrected: 3
    Aggregate: Corrected: 248
```

leo: 3 uncorrected is alarming. hardware-team looped in.

hardware-team: acknowledged. sending remote ops to run full hardware diagnostics and check DIMM/PCIe riser temps. May request node pull if uncorrected ECC persists.

ashwin: while hardware investigates, let's enable aggressive retry/fallback for the inference runtime: reduce max tokens, lower batch size, disable KV cache for these routes to reduce memory pressure.

olivia (oncall): patching runtime config: set `batch.max_tokens=512` and `runtime.kv_cache=false` for model:v2-large on the affected deployment group.

sre-bot: config rollout 2/3 succeeded, last rollout stuck on gpu-uw2-21 due to node drain—skipping.

jamie (support): customer alpha-suite reporting error spike: 7% 5xx. sending proactive note: "We are experiencing GPU node instability in us-west-2. Traffic is being shifted and we're investigating — ETA 2h." :rotating_light:

maria: capture flamegraphs and monitor memory alloc trends. Could be a firmware regression — what driver version are nodes on?

olivia (oncall): driver: 525.89.02 across cluster. No recent upgrades in the last 48h.

leo: check kernel messages for PCIe link errors too. I saw some `AER` messages earlier.

olivia (oncall): collecting:
```
[ 1233.112233] pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[ 1233.112345] NVRM: Xid 31, MMU fault, client 0b
```

ashwin: okay — mixes Xid 31/79/43 suggests both MMU and ECC/PCIe-level issues. prioritize hardware for inspection. We should also consider temporarily shifting pods to instance types without those GPUs if hardware team requests node pull.

hardware-team: we've scheduled a rack-level inspection. Ops will power-cycle and run memtest overnight if we see replays.

olivia (oncall): coordination note: if node pull needed, we prefer rolling replacement to keep capacity. I've requested two spare nodes in the pool.

sre-bot: Incident timeline updated. Incident severity: Sev-1 -> active. Runbook step: notify SRE leads and pager duty next-level.

maria: post-mortem checklist: collect crashdumps, driver logs (`/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`), kernel oops, eviction timestamps, and container logs for impacted images.

jamie (support): I'll consolidate customer notices and update the status page. Let me know if we start node replacements — that'll increase latency for queued jobs.

olivia (oncall): immediate action list:
- drain + isolate the 3 nodes (done)
- redirect traffic to us-east-1 (in progress)
- reduce runtime memory pressure (applied)
- collect diagnostics & hand off to hardware (in progress)
- notify customers (jamie)

leo: temp workaround idea: enable `fallback_model: v2-medium` for alpha-suite only — halves memory footprint and keeps availability. Can we do that quickly?

ashwin: yes, create route-level policy and pin alpha-suite to v2-medium for the next 4 hours.

olivia (oncall): did it. alpha-suite now routed to v2-medium. error rate dropped to 1.2% in the last 2 minutes.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: escalated to hardware-team and infra-leads. Next update due +30m.

jamie (support): posting initial status update to customers now. keeping them informed.

hardware-team: remote ops found one node with elevated VRM temps and one with a bad PCIe riser. Replacing riser on gpu-uw2-21, running memtest on gpu-uw2-17.

olivia (oncall): please keep the channel updated. I'll prepare the incident blameless post-mortem template once we stabilize.

ashwin: once hardware confirms replacements, let's plan a controlled driver restart and verify ECC counters reset.

maria: note for postmortem: correlate model batch sizes and KV cache usage with ECC events to see if certain prompts trigger more allocations.

olivia (oncall): thanks all. next update in ~25m or when hardware confirms node repair. :white_check_mark:
